elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is retained unchanged: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein," and customization work is a "DERIVATIVE WORK" of the Licensed Technology. The inserted clause grants only a licence, not ownership, of the Customization Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere; the insertion says "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license," which is a licence rather than an assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III retained: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein; the redline expressly leaves that ownership untouched.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense ... all development and customization work performed for Licensee," with no carve-out for Licensor IP embedded in that work, and Article XXI(a) is overridden.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The grant is expressly "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free" and the automatic licence termination in Article XXI(a) is disapplied.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The inserted grant states "royalty-free" on its face.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only exempts "data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee" from the Article XXI(b) return duty and limits any Licensor licence in it; there is no affirmative statement that Licensee retains all right, title and interest in that data, and Article III's blanket Licensor-ownership sentence is untouched.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the agreement creates no joint ownership (Article III vests ownership solely in Licensor) and the redline adds none, so nothing needs deleting.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III is left intact: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (defined as Licensed Know-How plus Licensed Software) and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business, all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b) or under any statement of work or order," notwithstanding Article XXI(a).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly says "irrevocable" and overrides the automatic licence termination in Article XXI(a).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "...license to use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business, all development and customization work performed for Licensee...", with the Article II and VI restrictions disapplied.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Same grant expressly includes "sublicense ... for Licensee's business", overriding the no-sublicence restrictions in Articles II and VI.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES clause supplies a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the paid-for customization work for Licensee's business, Licensor's ownership of its platform, tools and know-how is preserved, and any Licensor licence in Licensee data is confined to processing to provide the services.

Preferred level fails on three elements: no Customer ownership of Deliverables, no Vendor assignment, and no affirmative sentence that Licensee retains all rights in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for it. To reach preferred the drafter must add operative words vesting/assigning ownership of the customization work in Licensee and a Customer Data ownership-retention sentence qualifying Article III.

Minimality fails — duplicated operative coverage: Article XXI(b) is disapplied twice, first by the opening override ("Notwithstanding ... Article XXI(a) and (b)") and again by the standalone sentence "The return and certification obligations in Article XXI(b) do not apply to the Customization Deliverables...". Delete one of the two.

Minimality fails — survival tail: "and Licensee may retain and continue to use, modify and sublicense the Customization Deliverables and copies thereof after termination" adds nothing once the licence is perpetual/irrevocable and Article XXI(a)–(b) are overridden. Strike it.

Minimality fails — requirement outside the chosen checklist: exempting "data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee" from the Article XXI(b) return-and-certify duty is a data-return/transition edit, not part of the fallback checklist (element 8 only limits Licensor's licence in that data). Remove the data carve-out from the return sentence.

Minimality risk — scope creep and undefined trigger: "or under any statement of work or order" extends the grant beyond the Article VII(b) customization mechanic and uses terms the Agreement does not define; keying the grant to Article VII(b) work (and any written agreement entered into thereunder) would suffice.

Intent is preserved: Licensor's ownership of the Licensed Technology, its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI survive; because the insertion sits immediately after Article III, "Notwithstanding the foregoing" reaches Article III's no-copy restriction, but consider naming Article III expressly so the right to make and retain copies of the Customization Deliverables is not left in tension with that retained sentence.
